description: Build the four public marketing pages the fixed navbar points to: /product, /pricing, /for-developers, /self-host. Each is a new App Router route at the top level of web/src/app (public, OUTSIDE the (app) auth group), rendering the shared <SiteHeader/> and <SiteFooter/> from FEAT-002 and using only design-token classes and ui primitives. ROUTING NOTE (important): the authenticated dashboard already owns the URL /developers via web/src/app/(app)/developers/page.tsx (a route group's parentheses add no URL segment, so it resolves to /developers and is linked from the dashboard sidebar). Creating a second page at web/src/app/developers/page.tsx would resolve to the SAME /developers path and make Next.js fail the build with a 'two parallel pages resolve to the same path' error. Therefore the PUBLIC developers marketing page must live at web/src/app/for-developers/page.tsx (URL /for-developers); the nav label stays 'Developers'. FEAT-002's SiteHeader and SiteFooter already point the Developers link to /for-developers. Copy must attract the open-source community without sounding greedy, and MUST obey the honest-marketing discipline in docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/COMPETITIVE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md: everything is currently free, only clicks are counted (links/QR/edits/engagement-data/domains are unlimited and unmetered), privacy is first-class (no tracking cookies, no IP stored for geo, k-anonymity floor of 5, tracking pixels declined), MIT licensed and self-hostable in one command. Do NOT invent paid tiers, fake Enterprise 'contact us' pricing, a metered quota cap, a '31ms median redirect' number, or a 'scanned on creation' claim. Depends on FEAT-002 (shared header/footer + nav targets).
steps: For EACH page, create web/src/app/<route>/page.tsx (routes: product, pricing, for-developers, self-host - NOTE the developers page MUST be at for-developers, NOT developers, because /developers already exists in the (app) group and a second page at that path breaks the build). Each file exports a default React component that renders <SiteHeader/> at the top and <SiteFooter/> at the bottom, with the page body wrapped in the same container the landing page uses (max-w-[1080px] mx-auto px-6, appropriate vertical padding). Export `metadata` with a `title` on each page (the root layout template turns it into '%s · SnapURL'), e.g. Product -> 'Product', Pricing -> 'Pricing', Developers -> 'Developers', Self-host -> 'Self-host'. Pages can be server components; only add "use client" if a page needs interactivity.

PRODUCT PAGE (web/src/app/product/page.tsx): A feature overview that expands the six landing feature themes (Your domain your links; Route by anything / edge rules; Analytics without cookies; QR that stays correct; Trust made visible / the + preview; Built for automation). Reuse Card/CardBody and the icon-in-accent-wash tile pattern from the landing page. IMPORTANT: include a section with `id="analytics"` (so /product#analytics anchors to it) describing the cookieless analytics honestly: country/city/device/browser/referrer/conversions/QR-scans/unique-visitors, measured with a daily-rotating hash, no IP stored, city resolved from CloudFront edge header with a five-click k-anonymity floor (cities under the floor fold into 'Other cities'), uniques reset at 00:00 UTC. State plainly that tracking pixels are declined on principle and that POST /conversions + webhooks serve attribution server-side. Only claim features the product actually has per COMPETITIVE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md 'Already covered by SnapURL' list. End with a Start free CTA (next/link to /register).

PRICING PAGE (web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx): The honest anti-metering pitch. State clearly that SnapURL is currently free and that the only thing counted is clicks - links, custom aliases, QR codes, destination edits, tags/folders, custom domains, team members and 'engagement data' are unlimited and unmetered on every plan. Do NOT render fake paid tiers, a fake Enterprise/'contact us' plan, or a quota-cap gauge. A single honest 'Free' card (or a comparison framed as 'what we count vs what everyone else meters') is appropriate; the framing from the landing 'Everyone else meters four things. We count one.' is the right voice. Optionally include a short, honest self-host angle: if you self-host, you run it on your own infrastructure and there is no SnapURL bill at all. Include a Start free CTA and a link to /self-host. If a comparison table is used, only compare against InApp/typical-shortener metering patterns that are backed by docs/COMPETITIVE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md; do not fabricate competitor numbers.

DEVELOPERS PAGE (web/src/app/for-developers/page.tsx, URL /for-developers): Aimed at developers and the automation story. Cover the REST API, typed SDKs, real-time webhooks, a CLI, and the MCP server (these are the automation capabilities the landing page already names). Mention API keys and webhooks (in the 'Already covered' list). You MAY include short illustrative code snippets (e.g. a curl POST to create a link, a webhook payload shape) rendered in font-mono within a bg-surface-2/bg-surface-3 token-styled block - keep them plausible and generic, do NOT invent specific endpoint contracts beyond what web/README.md documents (e.g. POST /links returns a Link). Emphasize the open-source, self-hostable, MIT-licensed nature. End with CTAs to /register and /self-host. Note: this is the PUBLIC marketing /developers page and is unrelated to the authenticated dashboard developers route under (app)/developers - do not import from or modify the (app) route.

SELF-HOST PAGE (web/src/app/self-host/page.tsx): The strongest OSS-community pitch, in the honest voice of well-known open-source SaaS (self-host vs cloud framing that is not greedy). Lead with 'MIT licensed - self-host in one command' (already the landing badge). Explain the philosophy from docs/DECISIONS.md: short links that outlive your subscription, you own your data, no vendor lock-in, export everything always, no tracking cookies, cost-conscious architecture (built to run cheaply - e.g. SQS free tier over Redis, CloudFront edge geo instead of a licensed GeoIP DB) framed as user benefit not internals dump. Present a clear self-host-vs-cloud comparison that is honest: cloud is currently free and managed for you; self-host means you run it yourself with full control and no SnapURL involvement. Do NOT promise a hosted paid plan or enterprise support that does not exist. Include a real GitHub link to https://github.com/DhananjayThomble/URL-Shortener-App and CTAs to /register (try the cloud) and the repo (self-host).

Ensure every page uses only token utility classes (bg-surface, text-ink-2, border-line, bg-accent, bg-accent-wash, etc.), reuses Button/Card/Chip/SectionLabel from web/src/components/ui, and follows the bracketed-value Tailwind style of the landing page so all pages theme correctly in light and dark. Keep the OSS-community tone confident, specific, privacy-forward and non-greedy; when in doubt prefer the understated, backed claim.

Do a final read-through of all four pages against docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/COMPETITIVE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md to ensure no unbacked claim slipped in (no metered cap, no fake tiers, no 'scanned on creation', no specific redirect-ms number, no invented competitor data, no links to nonexistent routes).
acceptance_criteria: Four new routes exist and build as static pages: /product, /pricing, /for-developers, /self-host, each rendering the shared SiteHeader and SiteFooter.

The nav links from FEAT-002 all resolve: Product->/product, Analytics->/product#analytics (the Product page has an element with id='analytics'), Developers->/for-developers, Self-host->/self-host, Pricing->/pricing. No nav link 404s. The build must NOT error about two parallel pages resolving to /developers (the public developers page is at /for-developers).

Copy obeys the honest-marketing discipline: pricing shows everything is free with only clicks counted and NO fabricated paid/enterprise tiers or metered cap; analytics/privacy claims match docs (cookieless, no IP for geo, k-anonymity floor of 5, tracking pixels declined); no 'scanned on creation' claim; no specific 'ms median redirect' number; self-host page is MIT + one-command + own-your-data and links to the real GitHub repo.
All pages use design tokens (no hard-coded hex) and reuse ui primitives, rendering correctly in light and dark themes.
Each page sets a per-page metadata title.
`pnpm run type-check` passes and `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=... pnpm run build` succeeds, with the four new routes appearing in the route table.
verification: Confirm the build route table lists /product, /pricing, /for-developers, and /self-host (and still lists the existing /developers dashboard route without a duplicate-path error).
Grep the four new page files to confirm they contain no hard-coded hex colors (e.g. `#` followed by 3/6 hex digits in className) and that /product contains id="analytics".
findings: Created four public server-component pages under web/src/app: product/, pricing/, for-developers/ (URL /for-developers, NOT developers), and self-host/. Each renders <SiteHeader/> and <SiteFooter/> from @/components/marketing (FEAT-002), uses the landing container (max-w-[1080px] mx-auto px-6) and exports per-page metadata title. /product has id="analytics" (with scroll-mt-24) for the nav's /product#analytics anchor. Copy follows the honest-marketing discipline: pricing is a single free card + 'what we count vs what everyone else meters' framing with no fake paid/enterprise tiers or quota cap; analytics section states cookieless, no IP stored, CloudFront city header, k-anonymity floor of 5, uniques reset 00:00 UTC, tracking pixels declined, POST /conversions + webhooks for attribution; developers page covers REST API/SDKs/webhooks/CLI/MCP/API keys with generic font-mono snippets; self-host page is MIT + one-command + own-your-data + cloud-vs-self-host, linking the real GitHub repo. No hard-coded hex colors (verified by grep) and only design-token utility classes + ui primitives (Card/CardBody/Chip/SectionLabel) used. Verification: `pnpm run type-check` exits 0; `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=... pnpm run build` succeeds with 20 routes total; route table lists /product, /pricing, /for-developers, /self-host as static and still lists the existing (app) /developers dashboard with no duplicate-path error. No backend/(app) files touched. REVIEW FIX (2026-08-29-180738-review.md, blocking issue 'Unbacked developer surfaces'): the /for-developers page previously advertised a CLI, typed SDKs and an MCP server as shipped capabilities, but no such code exists in the repo (apps/ has only api/redirect/worker; no sdk/cli/mcp package, no @snapurl/sdk in any package.json) and docs/COMPETITIVE-GAP-ANALYSIS.md 'Already covered by SnapURL' lists only 'API keys and webhooks' and 'Conversion tracking', NOT CLI/SDK/MCP. Per the honest-marketing discipline in docs/DECISIONS.md I narrowed the developer surface to what the product actually backs: (1) SURFACES array trimmed from six cards to three — REST API, real-time webhooks, scoped API keys (removed the 'Typed SDKs', 'CLI' and 'MCP server' cards); (2) metadata.description rewritten to name only REST API + webhooks + API keys; (3) hero subhead rewritten from 'A typed REST API, SDKs, real-time webhooks, a CLI and an MCP server ... let your agents ship links too' to 'A typed REST API, real-time webhooks and scoped API keys ... read every line of the source that does it.' Kept the backed content untouched: the curl POST /links snippet (returns a Link, per web/README.md), the conversion.recorded webhook payload, the POST /conversions attribution copy, the MIT/open-source card and the /register + /self-host CTAs. No new endpoint contracts invented. Confirmed by grep that the page no longer contains CLI/SDK/MCP/agents references. Out of scope per orchestrator briefing and left unchanged: the landing page 'Built for automation' feature card and the authenticated (app)/developers dashboard, which carry the same pre-existing product claims (another session's area). type-check and build both re-verified green after the edit; /for-developers still in the route table as static.
